title: Minneapolis Insulation Rebates 2026: Green Cost Share, Xcel and CenterPoint
desc: Minneapolis insulation and air sealing rebates for 2026: the city's Green Cost Share up to $5,000 or $14,000, Xcel's 40% rebate up to $3,000 and CenterPoint's $750 to $1,500 amounts.
badge: Up to $3,000 from a utility, plus the city
lead: Old homes lose heat through the attic, the walls and the edge of the floor, and Minneapolis has many old homes. Three programs pay toward fixing that: the city's Green Cost Share rebate, Xcel Energy and CenterPoint Energy. We read each one on October 6, 2026. The rules are strict about air sealing and about who does the work.
cards_heading: What insulation rebates pay in Minneapolis
cards_intro: Xcel and CenterPoint pay for work on a home that uses their service. The city rebate is open to single-family homes and buildings of up to four units inside Minneapolis.

cards.title: City of Minneapolis Green Cost Share
cards.amount: Up to $5,000 ($14,000 in a Green Zone)
cards.note: Covers attic, wall and rim joist insulation as well as heat pumps and other upgrades. Apply through the Center for Energy and Environment within 60 days of finishing.

cards.title: Xcel Energy air sealing
cards.note: Leaks must fall by at least 15 percent, proved by a blower door test before and after the work.

cards.title: Xcel Energy attic insulation
cards.note: The attic must start at an insulation level of R-19 or less and end at R-49 or more.

cards.title: Xcel Energy wall insulation
cards.note: The wall cavity must be empty before the work and reach R-11 or more after.

cards.title: CenterPoint air sealing and attic insulation
cards.note: $750 for air sealing alone, $1,300 for air sealing with attic insulation. Attic insulation alone earns nothing.

cards.title: CenterPoint wall insulation
cards.note: Plus $200 for the rim joist when done with another measure.

after_cards:
R-value in plain words

R-value is a number that says how well a material resists heat flow. A higher number means better insulation. Xcel asks that an attic go from R-19 or less to R-49 or more. If your attic is already above R-19, Xcel's attic rebate does not apply.
sections: Why insulation is a Minneapolis story

The Census Bureau's American Community Survey for 2020 to 2024 counts 209,080 homes in Minneapolis. 72% were built before 1980 and 43% before 1940. Only 18% went up in 2000 or later. Houses from before 1940 were often built with no insulation in the walls. About 40% of the city's homes are detached houses and about 12% are in buildings of two to four units, which are the types the city rebate covers.

With about 70% of homes heating with natural gas and 25% with electricity, a heat loss fix reduces either bill. The census table does not say which homes are insulated, so we cannot say how many still need work. An energy visit will tell you.
Start with a Home Energy Squad visit

The city recommends a Home Energy Squad visit before you plan projects, and the visit is not required for the rebate. The Xcel page lists two visit types. The Energy Saver visit costs $70 and the Energy Planner visit costs $100, with a blower door test, an infrared camera check of attic and walls and a written report. Income-qualified customers may qualify for a free visit. The visit is for homes with electric service from Xcel and gas from Xcel or CenterPoint.
Pick the stack that fits your house

Programs differ in what they ask. Xcel pays a share of the project cost, up to its cap, and needs the blower door test. CenterPoint pays a flat amount for each measure and requires air sealing for attic work. The city has a larger cap that includes other work. If your home uses both Xcel and CenterPoint, you may be eligible for each company's rebate on different work, but a rebate from one program may not be claimed again from another Xcel program, according to Xcel's rules. Ask each program whether it counts the work for you before you sign the contract.

Xcel also pays a $600 bonus when a qualifying heat pump follows within two years of qualifying insulation work. If you plan both, do the insulation first so the heat pump can be smaller.

Both utilities require approved installers. Xcel says only registered insulation contractors can file the rebate and that self-installed insulation does not qualify. CenterPoint lists its eligible installers by service area on its page. The city works through the Center for Energy and Environment, which helps you find contractors. Get more than one bid. The CenterPoint page recommends comparing bids to find competitive pricing and an installer you trust.
claim_heading: How to claim Minneapolis insulation rebates
claim_steps: Schedule a Home Energy Squad visit, or ask a participating contractor for an air leak test.
Choose a contractor who is on the list for the utility that serves your gas or electricity.
Have the contractor do the blower door test before and after.
Ask the contractor to file the Xcel or CenterPoint rebate for you.
Apply to the city within 60 days of finishing the work.
faq: How much can I get for insulation in Minneapolis?

Xcel can pay up to $3,000 for air sealing plus attic and wall insulation, CenterPoint up to about $3,000 with all measures, and the city up to $5,000, or $14,000 in a Green Zone, across all projects. Which apply depends on who serves your home.
Does attic insulation alone earn a rebate?
Not from CenterPoint. Its page says attic insulation only has no rebate. Xcel requires air sealing with attic or wall insulation.
Do I need a blower door test?
For Xcel's rebate, yes, before and after. A blower door test uses a fan in a doorway to measure how leaky a home is.
Is the city rebate only for low-income homes?
No. The city rebate page asks that your home is in Minneapolis and is a single-family home or a building with two to four units. The loan has an income limit.
